newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium hit by new rail strike.
newsitem.headline: Belgium hit by new rail strike.

text.p: Train traffic came to a standstill in a major part of Belgium on Tuesday as two trade unions called their second 24-hour strike in a week over feared job losses.
"There is virtually no rail traffic in the provinces of Antwerp, Limburg and Hainaut," Belgian national railways NMBS/SNCB spokeswoman Leen Uytterhoeven told Belgian BRTN radio.
Unions fear the rail restructuring plans are in preparation for privatisation, and that their jobs could be at risk.
Most affected regions are the south west and north east of the country.

But Uytterhoeven said the Thalys high-speed Paris-Brussels-Amsterdam service and Eurostar were also affected and advised travellers to drive to the French city of Lille to board the international services to London and France.
There were no problems for international traffic to Germany, Luxembourg or Italy, she added.

Unions and management will meet after the strike which ends at 2000 GMT. A third 24-hour strike targeting the Brussels region has been pencilled in for Friday but may be called off if they can agree on an agenda for negotiations.
